surprises: THE BIG ONE — dairy is only ~5% of ARY's revenue and the campus's milk is almost certainly not bought here. Cross-group dairy = ₹44.78 L over 12m (205 active SKUs) against ₹8.96 Cr annualised = ₹75 per resident per MONTH. Loose milk moves ~21,700 L/yr ≈ 60 L/day for 5,000 people (12 ml/person/day), and packed milk adds only ~4,900 L. Two canteens, a hostel mess and a Gurdwara langar cannot run on that, so the institutional milk volume is being met outside ARY (Trust dairy/gaushala or direct canteen procurement) — that is a HYPOTHESIS, not verified: I did not check the purchase ledger or ask. It is the first thing to confirm, because it decides whether 'dairy expansion' here is a retail question or a supply-contract question.

Sales alone MISREAD availability — several zero-sale SKUs move in real volume by stock transfer to the counters: Pizza Cheese 1Kg 599.5 kg on 84 transfer lines, Delicious Butter 500 Gm 74 u on 26 lines, Super Matka Dahi 5Kg 16 buckets on 15 lines, Amul Fresh Cream 1 Ltr 17 u. Anything the canteens consume looks dead in a sales-only read. I re-classified mozzarella and bulk dahi as covered on this basis.

ZERO yogurt in 19,481 SKUs — no Epigamia, no Greek, no fruit yogurt, no probiotic dahi, no Yakult/Nutrifit/Prolife, no protein lassi or protein milk. The entire premium high-protein chilled shelf that is the national growth engine, and the one aimed straight at 18-25 Eternal University students, simply does not exist. ('yog' matches only yoga mats and Maha Yogi agarbatti.)

NO full-cream milk SKU of any kind (LIKE '%full cream%' → 0 rows; no Amul Gold) in a Punjabi-heritage Sikh institution — that is the milk families actually use for dahi, kheer, malai and karah prasad. Nor any A2/desi-cow, nor any lactose-free milk or curd.

Loose Desi Ghee alone is ₹13.89 L = 31% of the whole dairy lane and the biggest dairy SKU in the store — while every single BRANDED ghee SKU (Amul, Verka, Britannia, Dodla, Mahaan Cow, Shraddha) sold zero. There is also no 5 L or 15 L tin SKU, which is the langar/karah-prasad format on a Sikh campus.

Infant formula has sold NOTHING for ~2 years: 9 Lactogen SKUs listed, all zero in 12m, and all-time sales are 6 tins ending 2024-09-06. Nine dead SKUs is not stock — it is a shelf label. In a township 30-50 km from a market with married-staff families, this is the one gap that is a family emergency rather than a lost sale (and the IMS Act 1992 bans promoting it, so it will never sell itself off a shelf).

Dormancy in dairy is worse than the store average: 205 active dairy SKUs, only 71 sold in 12 months — 65% dead listings. ARY's own coverage report puts the Dairy Products group at 36.6% dead, but that group is only 41 SKUs and ₹9.31 L; it misses butter/cheese/curd (Confectionery), flavoured milk (Drinks), whitener (General Items), ghee (Oil & Ghee) and loose milk (Mini Meals).

DATA ODDITY — dairy is scattered and mis-filed across 13 groups, so any group-scoped dairy report understates the lane by ~5×: butter/cheese/curd sit under CONFECTIONERY, whitener under General Items, Amul Shrikhand under Drinks > Flavoured Milk, Verka Cow Milk 1 Litre and Amul Cow Ghee under OIL & GHEE, Amul Paneer 1 Kg under EDIBLE OIL & GHEE, Amul Butter 10Gm and Verka Butter 8G under GENERAL ITEMS > PEANUT BUTTER, and Amul Paneer 200 Gm / Verka Paneer 200Gm under Dairy Products > PACKED MILK.

A second own-label fresh counter runs in parallel: the '_Z' SKUs (Milk_Z ₹3.82 L, Dahi_Z ₹2.26 L, Paneer_Z ₹2.23 L, Khoya_Z ₹29.5 k), brand 'Ary', all selling out of the BASEMENT warehouse and duplicating the Ary Pos SKUs (Loose Milk, Super Dahi, Paneer Ls). Together the loose/own-label counter is ₹18.7 L = 42% of the dairy lane — ARY's fresh counter, not its packed shelf, is its dairy business.

Plant-based is ahead of lactose-free here: Sofit Soya Milk sells in 3 variants (~₹2.2 k each) while there is no lactose-free milk or curd at all. Also present and not on the ideal list: Amul Badam Shakers 200 Ml (₹4,750), Britannia Sweet/Mango Lassi 180 Ml (₹7,840 combined), Nestle Milky Bar Choo (₹4,190), a large Cerelac baby-cereal range (mostly dormant, ~₹3.9 k total), and 412 ice-cream SKUs incl. Amul Lactose Free Vanilla and mawa/rabri kulfis — the frozen dairy dessert business is far bigger than the chilled dairy business.
